description.value: The study examined habenula resting-state functional connectivity in autistic and neurotypical individuals, including diagnostic group differences, age-related developmental variability, and associations with autism-related phenotypic measures.

design.value: A multisite, cross-sectional resting-state functional MRI study using whole-brain habenula seed-based functional connectivity analyses in autistic and neurotypical participants, with group comparisons, age-by-group interaction analyses, and exploratory associations with phenotypic measures.

spans.text: Participants for the current study were selected from the large-scale, multisite ABIDE I and II datasets.

spans.text: Data were preprocessed using fMRIPrep 23.1.3, which utilizes the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) to ensure high-quality preprocessing with minimal user intervention ( 39 , 40 ).

We then used MRIQC 23.1.0 to inspect, flag, and remove participants, sessions, or runs ( 39 ) if they had excessive head motion defined by a framewise displacement greater than 0.35mm or had less than 100 usable time points following motion censoring ( 41 ).
